reasoning_summary: The deterministic verdict is INCONCLUSIVE with no failed checks. I can't ACCEPT, because the mesh, time and domain components are unmeasured for both Cd and St. I can't REJECT, because no FAIL exists.

R0 passes the averaging and statistics components. Mean Cd is 1.3278 as reported and 1.3277 in the stationary window. The Cd 95% CI is 1.0366e-05, and the averaging uncertainty is 7.057e-05. The St averaging uncertainty is 4.994e-06.
The averaging and statistics results are internal-consistency measures only. They say nothing about the discretisation or truncation error of R0.

The mesh is the least-verified part. R0 has 54244 cells, a representative cell size of 0.47033 D, a last wake cell of 0.96749 D, and 150 streamwise wake cells over a 60 D downstream length. Wake resolution drives both the shedding frequency and the mean drag, and it has never been tested.
The recorded time step is small enough to be a lower-priority risk. R0 uses backward time stepping with 872.03 steps per shedding period, and its max Courant number is 0.64796.
The domain is large relative to the body. R0 has 40 D upstream, 60 D downstream, 60 D half-height, and a blockage ratio of 0.0083333. The domain error is probably small, but it is unmeasured.

The St frequency resolution is 0.013334 against St = 0.16382, about 8% of the value. That is coarser than the 3% tolerance, so the St estimate relies on peak interpolation. Both the FFT and the reported St give 0.16382, but the resolution limit is a separate risk. RUN_LONGER would address it after the mesh question.
Budget is ample: 0 of 6 experiments and 0 of 12 compute units are used. REFINE_MESH from R0 costs an estimated 8677 s.
missing_evidence: Mesh discretisation error for mean_drag_coefficient and strouhal_number (no REFINE_MESH run)
Temporal discretisation error for both quantities (no REDUCE_TIME_STEP run)
Domain truncation/blockage error for both quantities (no EXPAND_DOMAIN run)
Strouhal frequency resolution (0.013334) is coarse relative to the 3% tolerance. A longer record would be needed to confirm St independently of the bin width.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The R0 mesh, especially the wake region (last wake cell 0.96749 D, representative size 0.47033 D), is too coarse. This would shift mean Cd or St by more than the 1.5% component budget (0.5 x 3%).
hypotheses.test: Refine the mesh by factor 1.4142 and compare Cd and St against R0. Changes well below 1.5% support the hypothesis being false. A change near or above 3% means the mesh is inadequate.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The time-step error (872 steps per period, backward scheme) is below 1.5% for both quantities.
hypotheses.test: Run REDUCE_TIME_STEP with factor 2 on R0 and compare Cd and St.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Boundary truncation (40 D / 60 D / 60 D, symmetryPlane sides) changes Cd and St by less than 1.5%.
hypotheses.test: Run EXPAND_DOMAIN with factor 2 and compare Cd and St.

next_experiment.reason: Mesh resolution is the most likely unmeasured error source. The wake cells are coarse, and Cd and St both depend on wake resolution. The estimated cost of 8677 s is affordable. A refinement result will show whether the R0 values hold within tolerance, and it starts the refinement sequence.
next_experiment.expected_outcome: If Cd and St change by well under 1.5% relative to R0 (Cd 1.3277, St 0.16382), the mesh component can be bounded and the time and domain checks follow. A change approaching or exceeding 3% means R0 is mesh-dependent and the sequence continues with a further refinement, or the system reports a FAIL.
